transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 PDT, duration ~48 mins. Attendees: Maya (AE), Raj (SE), Ben (SRE - AuroraPay), Leila (ML Eng), Samir (Eng Mgr).

Summary block (auto): quick numbers snapshot, tuning notes, agreed sweeps and deliverables.

[00:00] Maya: okay let's get started, thanks everyone for carving time. we ran the evening run and the morning steady state so we have a couple of charts to review.
[00:14] Raj: yep i'll share my screen in a sec, um quick hi to ben and team, thanks for the traffic replay. 
[00:22] Ben: hey all, yeah thanks, reality is the weekend spikes are the pain point for us so we tried to capture that in the replay. 
[00:30] Leila: quick note, we also pushed new input pretokenization so token counts skew a bit higher than last week.
[00:38] Maya: noted, that explains the higher tokens per request in the CSV. ok raj, screen?
[00:45] Raj: yeah opening the throughput dashboard — first slide is steady-state 4k token end-to-end run, concurrency 12, continuous batching on, max_batch_size 32, batch_timeout 40ms. steady-state throughput ~380 tokens/sec per GPU, p95 latency ~220ms, p99 ~540ms.
[01:07] Ben: that p99 is slightly worse than our SLO target, we shoot for 400ms p99.
[01:12] Raj: understood. when we bumped concurrency to 24 we saw median throughput increase but p99 shot up to 1.2s and queue depth grew — head-of-line blocking from long responses.
[01:26] Samir: so it's a tradeoff, higher concurrency gives better aggregate but more tail. is there an auto fallback you recommend?
[01:33] Maya: yes we can do route policy fallback to a smaller model for overflow or use burst capacity but both have cost/quality tradeoffs. also tuning batch_timeout and max_batch_size helps.
[01:43] Leila: curious, did you try prefix / KV caching? some of our prompts share big common preambles.
[01:48] Raj: we enabled KV caching on the model variant in the last run; it shaved about 12% off average token compute. but it didn't fix tail latencies when many long requests coincided. could be packer inefficiency.
[02:05] Ben: there were spikes where a single 12k token request blocked smaller 1.5k requests in the same micro-batch.
[02:12] Raj: yeah that was head-of-line. possible mitigations: request-size bucketing, dynamic packer that rejects mixing >x tokens in same batch, or split long requests into streaming chunks.
[02:25] Maya: and continuous batching parameters — lowering batch_timeout from 40ms to 20ms might reduce head-of-line at the cost of batch utilization.
[02:33] Samir: what about concurrency targets? the sweet spot seemed 8-16?
[02:37] Raj: in our sweep 8 gave low tails but lower throughput (~260 tps), 12 balanced throughput and tails, 16 started increasing tails again. 24 was unstable.
[02:50] Leila: do you have GPU utilization numbers? we want to understand whether it's compute bound or kernel saturation.
[02:55] Raj: GPUs were at 73% avg at concurrency 12, jumps to 92% at 24 but with more context switches and higher mmap. the kernel scheduler appears to thrash when batch sizes vary wildly.
[03:10] Ben: any quick config we can flip in pilot to try tomorrow?
[03:12] Maya: yes — three quick knobs: reduce batch_timeout to 20ms, cap max_batch_size to 24 for mixed-size pack, and enable request size bucketing for >6k token requests to separate them.
[03:24] Raj: i'll run a sweep matrix: concurrency [8,12,16,24], max_batch_size [16,24,32], batch_timeout [15ms,20ms,40ms], and with/without KV cache, then post CSVs.
[03:38] Samir: do you expect steady-state cost to go up if we reduce batch_timeout?
[03:42] Maya: a bit yes — smaller batches mean more kernel launches and slightly higher per-token cost, but if it keeps you within p99 SLO it's worth it. we can quantify cost delta in the spreadsheet.
[03:52] Ben: what about backpressure at the ingress? we saw queuing on our side when Redwood returned 503s or throttles.
[03:58] Raj: we hit transient application-level backpressure when the serving queue hit max capacity. recommended is client-side retry with jitter and token-based shaping to smooth bursts. and on Redwood side we can configure a soft-cap queue with early rejection to avoid full head-of-line collapse.
[04:16] Leila: any thoughts on streaming vs full-response for our UX? short streaming would reduce perceived latencies.
[04:21] Maya: streaming helps perceived latency for long generations but does not reduce server-side token compute; it can reduce p95 perceived but p99 server still relevant for SLOs.
[04:31] Ben: ok can we try streaming for the 12k long jobs and bucket short jobs separately?
[04:36] Raj: yes, route long jobs to streaming-optimized model variant and short jobs to low-batch-queue variant. that requires routing policy change in the config and minor SDK flag.
[04:46] Maya: i'll add that to the config change list.
[04:48] Raj: quick note on KV/prefix cache — we saw 10-14% token compute wins when prefix matching was high, but cache invalidation cost sometimes added jitter. tune TTL and shard counts.
[05:01] Samir: what's the recommended concurrency cap then?
[05:04] Raj: for your traffic mix i'd recommend initial concurrency cap 12 with autoscale up to 16 only if p99 stays under 600ms; otherwise scale horizontally by adding GPU workers.
[05:16] Ben: ok that seems sane. on cost questions, can you put model variant pricing side-by-side with expected tps cost?
[05:23] Maya: yes that's in the spreadsheet i'll send, plus the delta for burst capacity and fallback model usage.
[05:29] Leila: about the logs — can you mark the traces where H O L blocking occurred so we can correlate with trace ids?
[05:35] Raj: i'll annotate and upload traces with tags like "hol-event" and include short seg IDs.
[05:42] Samir: timeline — what's our plan this week to validate?
[05:45] Maya: run the full sweep, evaluate weekend traffic replay, adjust batch_timeout and bucket rules, then reconvene next Tuesday.
[05:52] Ben: ok. any security or private deployment concerns if we expand to private?
[05:56] Maya: separate convo but quick: private needs KMS review, VPC peering, and we can do SOC2 artifact handoff. we'll schedule a compliance call if you want.
[06:06] Ben: yes please.
[06:08] Maya: cool. check-ins: raj (perf runs), maya (pricing and config), ben (traffic shape & SLO).
[06:15] Raj: i'll kick off the concurrency/batch sweeps tonight and aim to upload results by Thursday.
[06:20] Leila: one more nuance — some of our inputs include binary-ish sections which inflate tokenization unpredictably, might want to pre-split or remove.
[06:29] Raj: good catch, we'll add a preprocessing step to clip or chunk those segments.
[06:34] Samir: should we also try quantized model variant to reduce GPU cost?
[06:38] Maya: yes we can test a 4-bit quantized variant; expected compute drop but maybe slightly worse quality. we'll include quality checkpoint in the sweep.
[06:47] Ben: perfect. I think that's it from my side.
[06:50] Maya: thanks everyone — recap in the notes and i'll drop the spreadsheet and the pilot dashboard. see you next week.

Auto notes: attached artifacts referenced - throughput-dashboard link (internal), pilot-telemetry-csv, pricing-throughput-spreadsheet.

End of transcript.
